events.text: {npc} finds you on a temple step with a chipped bowl and a lump of cold rice. "Every beggar on this bridge is an ear," {he} says. "Put your ear with ours. Tie a knot in this cord for every thing worth knowing, and leave it under the third lantern. Feed us, and we feed you."

effects.log: {npc} grins with half {his} teeth. "Welcome to the largest sect under heaven," {he} says, "and the poorest."
"People who never go hungry," {npc} says, "and never forget."

events.text: The ferryman will not take your coin. {npc} takes you across for nothing and talks the whole way about the price of everything on the river: salt, lives, the names of who crossed last night. "The Five Gates buy what you hear," {he} says at the far bank. "And we buy it twice if you hear it first."

effects.log: {npc}'s hand is wet from the oar and very strong. You are an errand runner of the Five Gates.

choices.text: Ask what happens to an ear that sells to two gates

effects.log: {npc} laughs. "It sells to three," {he} says. "Then the river has it."

events.text: A moth lands on your lamp, and a voice behind the paper screen says your name. {npc} never shows {his} face. "The Court does not pay in silver," {he} says. "It pays in debts. One day a moth will come to your lamp and ask you for something. Until then, tell us what the lamps see."

effects.log: The lamp gutters. When it steadies, the moth is gone, and so is {npc}.
"Small things," says {npc}. "Always small things. Until the last one."

events.text: {npc} reads your report twice, then holds it over the brazier until it curls. "Good," {he} says. "Now forget it. An ear that remembers what it sold is an ear somebody can squeeze."

effects.log: You try. Part of you never quite does.

choices.text: Ask who will read it now

effects.log: {npc} looks at you the way a fence looks at a ring. "Nobody you will ever meet."

events.text: The drop is empty when you go to it. Under the loose brick, instead of {npc}'s silver, there is a single word scratched in charcoal: wait. You wait three days. On the fourth {npc} arrives limping, with a new drop and a story {he} does not tell.

effects.log: {npc} nods. "That is why you are still alive," {he} says, and pays you double.
"A rival network found the old drop," {npc} says. "It was nearly you."

events.text: {npc} shares a bowl of noodles with you in a stall by the canal and talks about everything except the work. A child of {his} is learning letters; a roof leaks. At the end {he} slides the bill toward you. "The network pays," {he} says, "but not for friendship."

effects.log: {npc} smiles properly for the first time since you met.
{npc} pays for {his} own, exactly, to the last copper.

events.text: {npc} gives you a cord with two knots already tied in it. "You run now," {he} says. "Not from anyone. Between people. A runner who reads the letters {he} carries does not run for long."

choices.text: Swear you will not read them

effects.log: {npc} believes you, or pretends to.
You both know you will read every one.

events.text: Your own corner of the city now: three streets, a market and the people in them, and the ears who listen there report to you before they report to {npc}. "Be fair with them," {he} says. "An ear you starve will sell you to anyone with a bun."

effects.log: {npc} writes something in a ledger you are not allowed to see.

choices.text: Ask what happened to the last one

effects.log: "Ask the river," {npc} says.

events.text: You are given a seat at the back table, where the elders of {inw_net} sit and decide which secrets are worth a life. {npc} pulls the chair out for you. "From here," {he} says, "there is only one chair higher, and it is not empty."

effects.log: The chair is hard and very old. You are {inw_rank}.
{npc} follows your eyes, and does not tell you not to.

events.text: {npc} has headed {inw_net} longer than you have been alive. {He} pours two cups of tea and pushes one across the ledger table. "Everyone in this room thinks you should have my chair," {he} says. "I would like to hear whether you think so too."

choices.text: Say you will take it, if you must

effects.log: {npc} sets down {his} cup. "Then take it," {he} says, and stands.

choices.text: Say the chair is {his} until {he} lays it down

effects.log: {npc} studies you a long while. "That is the right answer," {he} says, "and I do not trust it."

events.text: The elders of {inw_net} come to you one by one, at night, each with the same question in a different coat: how long will old {npc} live? It is not a question about medicine.

effects.log: You send word that you will meet {him} in the back room at dawn.
{npc} hears of it by morning. {He} sends you a jar of plum wine and no message.

events.text: {npc} gives you the key to the ledger chest with both hands, as one gives a tablet to the next of the blood. "I kept it forty years," {he} says. "Do not keep it so long. Nobody should know this much for so long."

choices.text: Promise to hand it on in time

effects.log: {npc} nods, and walks out into the morning without a guard for the first time in forty years.
"Everyone," {npc} says.

events.text: The elders of {inw_net} lay the old head's cord on the ledger table, knotted with every year of a life, and push it toward you. Nobody speaks. You are {inw_rank}, and the room is waiting for your first order.

effects.log: By the next moon every sign and every drop of the network is new. The elders look at one another, satisfied.

choices.text: Order the old head buried with honours

effects.log: Beggars, ferrymen and moths come out of every corner of the city for the funeral. You did not know there were so many.

events.text: Your network is a back room behind a tea stall, a cracked inkstone, one lamp and one ear. The tea seller wipes the counter and asks, without looking up, what you want to know first.

choices.text: The names of everyone who comes in

effects.log: By the end of the month you know them all, and one of them is not what they say.
Three other networks, it turns out. They know about you already.

events.text: You hang a paper crane in the window of {inw_net}, the sign that it is open for business. By morning there are two letters under the door. One asks for a price. The other says only: we see you.

effects.log: Your first client pays in old coins and does not give a name.
You burn it. A second one, in the same hand, comes the next night.

events.text: {npc} sells chestnuts at the busiest corner of the market and remembers every face that buys one. "I can tell you who walks with whom," {he} says, "and who walks alone when they think nobody sees."

effects.log: {npc} counts it twice, then gives you a chestnut for free.
{npc} shrugs. Chestnuts are paid by the bag too.

events.text: {npc} is a clerk in the magistrate's yamen with very clean sleeves and a very bad debt. "Every case passes my desk," {he} says quietly. "Every bribe passes my desk. I would like some of them to pass my purse."

effects.log: {npc} bows low enough to hide {his} face. A clerk who owes you is worth two who are paid.

choices.text: Pay {him} and let the debt stand

effects.log: {npc} takes it. A clerk in debt also keeps listening.

events.text: {npc} was an outer disciple of a great sect for nine years and was never once called to the inner hall. "I know the back gates," {he} says. "I know which elder drinks and which one prays. I know which disciple is about to betray them, because I almost did."

effects.log: {npc} smiles for the first time in nine years.
"Nobody asked me," {npc} says. "You did."

events.text: {npc} keeps a gaming house by the docks that is not, officially, a gaming house. Debtors talk. Thieves boast. "Night people," {he} says, "tell everything to whoever pours. I pour."

effects.log: {npc}'s grip leaves a little silver dust on your palm.

choices.text: Warn {him} not to sell to anyone else

effects.log: {npc} looks hurt, which is how you know {he} was going to.

events.text: {npc} brings you the week's notes, and a child holding {his} sleeve. "My sister's child," {he} says. "My sister is gone, and there is nobody else. The child will not talk. I thought: a house of ears is a good place for a child who does not talk."

effects.log: The child sweeps the back room and listens to everything. You have a second ear for the price of a bowl of rice.

choices.text: Tell {him} the work is too dangerous for a child

effects.log: {npc} takes the child home. {He} is quieter with you after that.

events.text: {npc} is sure {he} was followed home. {He} wants a week away from the drops, and silver to pay a cousin in the hills to hide {him}.

choices.text: Give {him} the week and the silver

effects.log: {npc} comes back after a week with a tan and a name: the one who followed {him}.
{npc} keeps working, looking over {his} shoulder at every corner.

events.text: A rival network has offered {npc} three times what you pay. {He} tells you so, and lays the offer on the table: a folded paper and a silver hairpin. "I am telling you," {he} says, "so you know what I am worth."

effects.log: {npc} pins the hairpin in {his} collar and keeps working for you.

fail.log: {npc} stays, and hates you for it.

events.text: {npc} has fallen in love with someone {he} was sent to watch. {He} confesses it with {his} eyes on the floor, as if it were a theft.

choices.text: Take {him} off the job, and wish {him} well

effects.log: {npc} cries, which surprises you both. The reports stay honest.
{npc} keeps watching. The reports get shorter.

events.text: {npc} brings you a rumour {he} paid for out of {his} own pocket: a name, a house, a date. It is the best thing your network has brought in all year, and {he} only wants the silver back.

effects.log: {npc} spends it on new boots and tells everyone where {he} got them. It is good for business.
{npc} nods. Fair is fair.

events.text: An old friend of {npc}'s from before the network turns up at the safehouse, drunk and asking for {him} by {his} real name. Two of your other ears are watching from the stairs to see what you do.

choices.text: Send the friend home with a coin and a lie

effects.log: The friend goes. {npc} thanks you without a word.
You move by morning. It costs a month of silver and nobody is careless again.
The friend is thrown out into the rain. {npc} does not look at you for a week.

events.text: Your people have watched {npc} spar, eat and sleep for a month. The numbers come written on a strip of paper as long as your arm: how {he} breathes, how far {he} reaches, how long {he} lasts. For the first time you know exactly how strong {npc} is.

choices.text: Read it twice and burn it

effects.log: It is on {npc}'s page in your People list now, and nowhere else.
You fold it into your sleeve. It feels heavier than paper.

events.text: "{npc} trains before dawn, alone, where nobody can see," the report says. "The art {he} shows in the open is not the art {he} trains." Your people have counted every step.

effects.log: You know now what {npc} really has.
You watch from the trees one cold morning. The report was right.

events.text: The second report on {npc} is about what {he} wants, not what {he} can do: the people {he} likes, the ones {he} does not, what {he} really thinks of you. It is not all kind.

effects.log: You know {npc} better than {his} own family does now.
You skip it. You read it later, alone.

events.text: The report on {npc} is short, and your informant brings it in person, which they never do. "{He} is planning something," they say. "Against you. {He} has been asking where you sleep."

choices.text: Thank them, and change where you sleep

effects.log: You sleep somewhere else for a season. {npc} goes on asking.
You stand in {npc}'s doorway and say nothing at all. {He} understands.

events.text: The last report on {npc} is the one nobody was ever meant to write. Your informant hands it over folded small, as if it were wet. Everything a person hides is in it.

effects.log: You lock it away. A secret kept is a secret that can still be sold, or used, or forgiven.

choices.text: Burn it, unread past the first line

effects.log: You burn it. You remember the first line anyway.

events.text: Your people have found what {npc} would kill to keep hidden. They wait to see what you will do with it, which is the thing they really came to learn about you.

choices.text: Say nothing will be done with it, yet

effects.log: Your people nod and go back to work. Yet is a word they understand.

choices.text: Tell them it is worth silver

effects.log: Your people smile. Now they know what kind of house this is.

events.text: Your people come back from the great house with ink on their fingers and a map of its back halls drawn from memory: who argues with whom, what the treasury holds, which elder leaves at night. A great house is a family, and every family has a cupboard.

effects.log: The dossier goes into the ledger chest, under the house's name.
"A cook who will not cook there again," your informant says.

events.text: The house's gatekeeper was easy. The house's steward was not, and your informant has a bruise across one cheek to prove it, but the books came out with them, every page copied.

effects.log: Your informant laughs and winces at the same time.
"Seen," says your informant. "Not known."

events.text: Your people follow the names on the list for a season: the master who drinks before duels, the one who has not fought in years, the one whose famous art is a mask for another. The storytellers sing one list. You have the real one.

effects.log: You study it until you could recite it, which you never will.

choices.text: Lock it away for a bad day

effects.log: You lock it in the ledger chest. Some day a name on it will come for you.

events.text: A bard sings the rankings in a teahouse, and every word is wrong. Your informant, sitting beside you, hums along and says nothing. You both know the true version now.

effects.log: It is a good song, even if it is a lie.
Two people in the teahouse know the real words. Neither sings them.

events.text: {npc} sits down across from you in the teahouse and pushes a heavy purse halfway across the table. "I want to know what goes on inside {inw_house}," {he} says. "Its halls, its silver, its quarrels. Not the songs. The truth."

effects.log: {npc} lets go of it. "Three years," {he} says. "No more."
{npc} takes it back without any sign of feeling. "There are other ears," {he} says.
"Because I am about to marry into it," {npc} says, "or go to war with it. I have not decided which."

events.text: {npc} does not come in person. A letter does, sealed with a seal you do not recognise, asking for the state of {inw_house} and naming a price no honest person would offer. A second note tied to it says: {npc} will collect.

effects.log: You send back a single brushstroke: yes.
You send back nothing. Some letters should not be answered.

events.text: {npc} has come back. {He} was pleased last time, {he} says, and has more work: {inw_house}, this time, and a little more silver. "I like an ear that does what it is paid for," {he} says, "and forgets who paid."

effects.log: {npc} pays half in advance, as before.

choices.text: Say you are full this year

effects.log: {npc} nods. "Next year, then."

events.text: You hand {npc} the dossier in a plain wrapper. {He} reads the first page standing up, then sits down to read the rest. When {he} looks up {he} is somebody who knows something, and you can see {him} deciding what to do with it.

choices.text: Do not ask what {he} will do

effects.log: {npc} pays the rest, and adds a little for your silence.
"Better that you do not know," {npc} says, "since you are the one who knows everything else."

events.text: {npc} pays the second half of the contract in a teahouse full of people, slowly, coin by coin, so that everyone sees {inw_net} keeps its word.

effects.log: Half the teahouse will have a contract for you by the next moon.

choices.text: Count it again in front of {him}

effects.log: {npc} laughs. The teahouse laughs with {him}. Nobody will cheat you soon.

events.text: A thing only your own people knew is being sung in a teahouse by the river: the name of a client, the price, the date. Someone in your house is selling. Every face at the morning meeting looks like a face that could.

effects.log: You watch. The one who sold watches you back, and you do not know which one it is.
It costs you a month and a great deal of silver. The leak stops for a while.

events.text: A rival's errand runner brushes past you in the market and murmurs the name of your last client, then laughs and is gone. It was not a threat. It was a receipt.

effects.log: You let it go, for now. You count your people again that night.
You lose the runner in the fish market, and find a dead drop that is not yours.

events.text: {npc} does not deny it. {He} sits in the back room with {his} hands on the table, very still. "They had my brother," {he} says. "Or they said they did. I did not know who to ask."

effects.log: {npc} stands, bows once, and walks out with nothing.
{npc} puts {his} head on the table and does not lift it for a long time.

choices.text: Keep {him} selling, and write what {he} sells

effects.log: {npc} understands at once. "They will kill me if they find out," {he} says. You both know it.

events.text: You lay the copied notes in front of {npc}, one by one, in the order {he} sold them. {He} watches them pile up and smiles a little at the end. "I always wondered how long it would take you," {he} says.

effects.log: {npc} goes laughing, which is somehow worse.
"Of course," {npc} says. "I sell to whoever is winning."

events.text: They pull your informant from the canal at dawn, and the river police are already paid to call it a drowning. A single moth has been pressed into the dead hand. It is a signature.

effects.log: You bury your ear on a hill above the city with your own hands. The rest of your people watch, and remember.
Your people hear you swear it. They work harder after that, and more carefully.

events.text: Your informant is found under a bridge where the beggars sleep, and not one of the beggars saw anything, which is how you know who did it. A knotted cord is tied around the dead wrist.

effects.log: You bury your ear with your own hands. The beggars on the bridge watch you do it and do not look away.

choices.text: Send the cord back to the bridge

effects.log: You hang it on the bridge rail. By morning it is gone.

events.text: Your informant comes home from the river in a ferry nobody rowed. The Five Gates do not sign their work. They do not need to.

effects.log: You bury your ear on a hill above the river.

choices.text: Pay the ferryman's guild a visit

effects.log: The guild serves you tea and tells you nothing at great length.

events.text: You wake to bells, and the sky over the safehouse is orange. By the time you get there it is ash and wet beams. Your notes, your silver, a year of listening. The fire spread to nothing else. Whoever set it was careful.

effects.log: You rent a new back room before the ash is cold. Your people see that you do not run.
You wait for the heat to pass, and the city to forget the smell of smoke.

events.text: The knife comes out of a crowd in the market, quick and low, and is gone again before you turn. It was meant to warn, not to kill. Whoever held it knew exactly where to put it.

effects.log: You keep walking, bleeding into your sleeve, so that whoever is watching sees you keep walking.
You do not leave the safehouse for a month.

events.text: {npc}, who speaks for the Beggars' Sect in this city, sends you a chipped bowl with a crack painted red. Everyone in the murim knows what it means. The beggars on every bridge will be watching your people now, and worse than watching.

choices.text: Send the bowl back, mended with gold

effects.log: {npc} keeps it, which means it is war anyway, but a respectful one.
Half the city hears it break.

events.text: A ferry drifts up to your landing with nobody aboard and five coins laid on its bench, face down. {npc} of the Five Gates is telling you the price of your network has been agreed, and it is not paid in silver.

effects.log: The coins go back down the river with an answer: come and take it.
You keep the coins. A war is expensive.

events.text: Every lamp in your safehouse is full of dead moths in the morning, hundreds of them, and a letter from {npc} that says only: the Court has called in your debt. You were not aware that you owed one.

effects.log: You light every lamp. Your people see the light, and stay.
You work in the dark for a season. It is, at least, safe.

events.text: The quiet war with {inw_foe} goes on: a courier who does not arrive, a drop found empty, a fire in a warehouse that was yours. {npc} sends no letters now. The city waits to see what you do this year.

effects.log: You give the order.

choices.text: Send {npc} silver and ask for peace

effects.log: You send the silver.

choices.text: Try to turn one of their ears

ok.log: You find one who will listen.

fail.log: The one you try goes straight to {npc}.

events.text: {npc} meets you in the open, on a bridge at noon, which is the one place neither network will strike. {He} offers you a pear. "We could both stop," {he} says. "Or we could both go on until one of us has no ears left."

choices.text: Take the pear, and the peace, for a price

effects.log: You name the price. {npc} names a higher one. You pay it.

choices.text: Throw the pear in the river

effects.log: {npc} watches it float away. "Then go on," {he} says.

events.text: Your informants bring you the name of {npc}'s best ear: a tailor who sews for half the great houses, and hears everything said during a fitting. The tailor has a child who wants to go to an academy the tailor cannot pay for.

effects.log: The tailor starts sewing your notes into the hems.
You give the order. You do not sleep well.

events.text: It ends in a teahouse. {npc} sets down a cup, pours you tea, and leaves without drinking. {inw_net} has won the quiet war, and every teahouse in the murim knows it by nightfall.

effects.log: It is very good tea. Nobody poisons tea in a teahouse in front of the whole city.

choices.text: Leave it, and pay for both cups

effects.log: The whole teahouse sees you pay. That is how the murim learns who won.

events.text: You count your people at the morning meeting and it does not take long. The rival network has the river now, and the bridges, and one of your safehouses with your sign still on the door.

effects.log: You start again, smaller and quieter. The best networks are always smaller than they look.

choices.text: Swear you will take it back

effects.log: Your remaining ears hear you swear it.

events.text: Neither network says the war is over. The couriers just start arriving again, and the fires stop. It is the kind of peace that has to be counted in years without funerals.

effects.log: You count the first one. It is a good year.

choices.text: Send the rival a jar of wine

effects.log: The jar comes back empty, washed and with a plum in it. It is a reply.

events.text: {npc} holds the ledger chest key the way you held it the first night: too tight. "What do I do first?" {he} asks.

effects.log: {npc} laughs, and you see the head of a network in the laugh.

choices.text: Tell {him}: forget what you know about me

effects.log: {npc} does not promise. That is how you know you chose well.

events.text: On the first morning of {sh_heir}'s rule over {sh_house}, three of your old ears come to you instead of to {sh_him}, out of habit. They stand in the doorway with their reports in their hands, waiting to see which way you point.

effects.log: They go. {sh_heir} hears of it, and thinks better of you.
They read them to you. {sh_heir} hears of it by noon.

events.text: A client with a great deal of silver wants {sh_house} to dig into the household of a prince. {sh_heir} is for it. The silver would pay every ear for three years. The prince would remember forever. {sh_His} message asks your will.

effects.log: The contract is taken under {sh_heir}'s name.

choices.text: Refuse it in your own name

effects.log: The client is sent away. The network knows whose word did it.
You send nothing. {sh_heir} decides alone.

events.text: A rival network has been killing {sh_house}'s ears on the river. {sh_heir} wants to pay for peace. The older ears want to burn the rival's warehouses, and they are asking whether you agree with them.

effects.log: The silver goes down the river. The killings stop.
The river is orange that night. {sh_heir} learns of the order from the smoke.

choices.text: Say it is not your network any more

effects.log: They go away disappointed.

events.text: {sh_heir} suspects a mole among the old ears, the ones who came to the network in your time. {sh_He} wants to put out every one of them at once, guilty or not. The old ears come to you.

choices.text: Back {sh_heir}: let the purge go ahead

effects.log: Your old ears are put out. One of them was the mole. The others were your friends.
The purge does not happen. {sh_heir} stops speaking to you at the morning meeting.
You let {sh_heir} decide. {sh_He} decides on half of them.

events.text: Your drop is empty. So is the next one, and the one after. {sh_heir} has changed every sign of {sh_house} without telling you, and the message, when it finally comes, is very polite: the network thanks its old head, and no longer needs to trouble {p_him}.

choices.text: Accept it, and let the network go

effects.log: You burn your old codebook in the brazier. It takes a long time.

choices.text: Go to the back room and take your chair back

effects.log: You go to the back room.

choices.text: Go to {sh_heir} alone and ask to talk

effects.log: You go alone, without a single ear.

events.text: You give {sh_heir} the last thing you kept back: a thin book of the names of the ears nobody else knows about, the ones who report only to the head. {sh_He} takes it with both hands. "Why now?" {sh_he} asks. Because there is nothing left that you want to know.

effects.log: {sh_heir} bows. When you leave, nobody follows you. It is the first time in years.
{sh_heir} understands anyway. {sh_He} walks you to the gate.
